question: Why do y'all, yinz and youse keep springing up in different English-speaking regions?
answer: Because standard English has no plural you. Thou was the singular and you the plural, until you displaced thou and left one word doing both jobs. Speakers keep rebuilding the lost plural: y'all in the American South, yinz, from you ones, around Pittsburgh, youse in Ireland, Liverpool and Australia. The same hole gets patched locally.
move: Where a language drops a distinction speakers need, they rebuild it locally.
source: Wales, Personal Pronouns in Present-Day English, 1996
reference: Wales, Personal Pronouns in Present-Day English, Cambridge University Press, 1996
